definition.def: A layer of a material or substance is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.
examples: A fresh layer of snow covered the street. [+ of]
Arrange all the vegetables except the potatoes in layers.

definition.def: If something such as a system or an idea has many layers, it has many different levels or parts.
examples: ...an astounding ten layers of staff between the factory worker and the chief executive. [+ of]
Critics and the public puzzle out the layers of meaning in his photos. [+ of]

definition.def: If you layer something, you arrange it in layers.
examples: Layer the potatoes, asparagus and salmon in the tin. [VERB noun]
By lifting and layering her hair, Michael created a lighter frame for her face. [VERB noun]

examples.sentence: During the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, the entire site became covered with a layer of hard grey clay, which minimised further erosion.
It was not until 1500 BC, however, that the first hollow glass container was made by covering a sand core with a layer of molten glass.
The wall of the fruit has three layers: a waterproof outer layer, a fibrous middle layer and a hard, inner layer.
The thick fibrous middle layer produces coconut fibre, 'coir', which has numerous uses and is particularly important in manufacturing ropes.
The woody innermost layer, the shell, with its three prominent 'eyes', surrounds the seed.
A two-metre-deep layer of soil was laid on top of the tunnel and the road above rebuilt.
While in the upper layers of the city, people could walk undisturbed between elegant palaces and streets, the lower layer was the place for services, trade, transport and industry.
At one time, all tennis rackets were strung with natural gut made from the outer layer of sheep or cow intestines.
Peatlands - wetlands with a waterlogged organic soil layer - are particularly targeted.
At the same time, sand was dredged from the waters and piled on top of the layer of stiff clay that the massive dredging had laid bare.
